section: Nature of 1857 - the historiographical debate (mutiny, feudal reaction, first war of independence)
subsections: Centenary histories - S.N. Sen and R.C. Majumdar

accepted.s: Which of the following historians characterised the uprising of 1857 as a purely military outbreak or a mere sepoy mutiny?
accepted.x: Sir John Lawrence, along with J.R. Seeley and Charles Raikes, regarded the uprising primarily as a sepoy mutiny and denied it a popular or national character.
accepted.tq: Match the historian with the distinctive verdict.

accepted.s: Who described the Revolt of 1857 as a conflict between civilisation and barbarism?
accepted.x: T.R. Holmes described the revolt as a conflict between civilisation and barbarism.
accepted.tq: Use the exact phrase to identify the associated historian.

accepted.s: The interpretation of the Revolt of 1857 as a war of fanatic religionists against Christians is associated with:
accepted.x: L.E.R. Rees interpreted the revolt as a war of fanatic religionists against Christians.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between historians whose interpretations concern religion and mutiny.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: T.R. Holmes — Conflict between civilisation and barbarism
Benjamin Disraeli — National rising, not a mere mutiny
S.N. Sen — War of fanatic religionists against Christians
accepted.x: The description of the revolt as a war of fanatic religionists against Christians was given by L.E.R. Rees. S.N. Sen stated that a fight for religion ended as a war of independence.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped historian and verdict.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding interpretations of the Revolt of 1857:
1. Benjamin Disraeli regarded it as a national rising rather than a mere mutiny.
2. Karl Marx regarded it as a national revolt.
3. V.D. Savarkar regarded it as a planned First War of Indian Independence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Disraeli, Marx and Savarkar rejected the narrow interpretation of the revolt as merely a sepoy mutiny, though Savarkar gave it the specific nationalist title.
accepted.tq: Check each historian against the precise nationalist interpretation.

accepted.s: The statement that the uprising essentially represented a feudal rising was made by:
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru described the uprising as essentially a feudal rising in The Discovery of India.
accepted.tq: Use the author-and-verdict association rather than the broader nationalist label.

accepted.s: “What began as a fight for religion ended as a war of independence” was the assessment of:
accepted.x: S.N. Sen concluded that the revolt began as a fight for religion but ultimately developed into a war of independence.
accepted.tq: Identify the historian from the famous concluding formulation.

accepted.s: With reference to the assessment of Indian nationalism in the middle of the nineteenth century, which of the following is correct?
o: It was rejected as embryonic by both R.C. Majumdar and S.N. Sen.
It had already become fully developed and uniform throughout India.
It was regarded as being only embryonic by R.C. Majumdar and S.N. Sen.
It was confined exclusively to the British army.
accepted.x: R.C. Majumdar and S.N. Sen both regarded Indian nationalism in the mid-nineteenth century as still embryonic.
accepted.tq: Avoid the extreme wording in the distractors and select the qualified description.

accepted.s: Which one of the following books was written by R.C. Majumdar?
o: The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857
Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies
accepted.x: R.C. Majumdar wrote The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857, published in 1957.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar 1857 titles by their authors.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Book)
A. Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies
B. The Great Rebellion
C. The Peasant and the Raj
D. Awadh in Revolt 1857-58

List-II (Author)
1. Eric Stokes
2. Ashok Mehta
3. Rudrangshu Mukherjee
4. S.B. Chaudhuri
accepted.x: Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies was written by S.B. Chaudhuri; The Great Rebellion by Ashok Mehta; The Peasant and the Raj by Eric Stokes; and Awadh in Revolt 1857-58 by Rudrangshu Mukherjee.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure book-author pair and eliminate the codes.

accepted.s: Who authored The Indian Mutiny of 1857?
accepted.x: The Indian Mutiny of 1857 was written by G.B. Malleson.
accepted.tq: Identify the author of the exact title, not the similar title The Great Mutiny.

accepted.s: The book The Great Mutiny is associated with which author?
accepted.x: Christopher Hibbert authored The Great Mutiny.
accepted.tq: Separate similar-sounding titles by matching the exact author.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between S.N. Sen's and R.C. Majumdar's centenary histories?
o: Majumdar's work was Government-commissioned, whereas Sen wrote independently outside the centenary project.
Sen's work was Government-commissioned, whereas Majumdar wrote independently after parting with the official project.
Both were official Government of India volumes and reached the same conclusion about independence.
accepted.x: S.N. Sen's Eighteen Fifty-Seven was the Government of India-commissioned centenary history. R.C. Majumdar wrote his 1957 work independently after parting with the official project.
accepted.tq: Compare the commissioning status and institutional context of the two works.
accepted.sec: Centenary histories - S.N. Sen and R.C. Majumdar

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the centenary histories of 1857:
1. S.N. Sen's Eighteen Fifty-Seven was published in 1957.
2. R.C. Majumdar's The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857 was also published in 1957.
3. Sen's interpretation was that the revolt began as a religious struggle and ended as a war of independence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Both books appeared in 1957, while Sen gave the revolt an evolutionary interpretation from a religious fight to a war of independence.
accepted.tq: Verify the common year first, then distinguish the two historians' verdicts.
accepted.sec: Centenary histories - S.N. Sen and R.C. Majumdar

accepted.s: R.C. Majumdar's interpretation of the Revolt of 1857 differs from the nationalist interpretation attributed to him in some classifications because he specifically argued that it was:
o: the first, national and completely successful war of independence
only a conflict between civilisation and barbarism
neither first, nor national, nor a war of independence
accepted.x: R.C. Majumdar's own verdict was that the revolt was neither the first nor national nor a war of independence, despite some classifications placing him in a broader nationalist school.
accepted.tq: Resolve the apparent contradiction by separating a school classification from the historian's own verdict.
accepted.sec: Centenary histories - S.N. Sen and R.C. Majumdar

accepted.s: The term 'Sepoy Mutiny' or 'Indian Mutiny' was predominantly used by which school of historians?
accepted.x: British or imperialist historians commonly used the labels Sepoy Mutiny or Indian Mutiny and denied the revolt a national character.
accepted.tq: Associate the label with the historiographical school that used it.

accepted.s: Which one of the following labels was particularly associated with Indian nationalist interpretations of the uprising of 1857?
accepted.x: Indian nationalist historians commonly used the label Great Rebellion, while First War of Independence was especially associated with V.D. Savarkar.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a broad nationalist label from the specific Savarkar formulation.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: V.D. Savarkar — First War of Independence
British or imperialist school — Sepoy Mutiny
Other names — Religious Fanaticism and Administrative Blunders
accepted.x: Revolt of 1857 and Indian Insurrection are listed as other names. Religious fanaticism and administrative blunders were explanations associated with the British or imperialist interpretation.
accepted.tq: Separate labels from explanatory causes in a school-wise classification.

accepted.s: The interpretation of the Revolt of 1857 as a feudal reaction primarily emphasises the role of:
o: dispossessed princes and taluqdars attempting to restore their lost positions
urban middle classes demanding representative government
European merchants opposing the East India Company
accepted.x: The feudal-reaction interpretation highlights dispossessed princes and taluqdars such as Nana Saheb, Lakshmibai and Begum Hazrat Mahal, who sought to recover lost positions.
accepted.tq: Apply the interpretation to the social groups and motives it highlights.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the limitations of describing the Revolt of 1857 as the First War of Independence:
1. There was no common goal among all the participants.
2. Modern nationalism had not yet emerged.
3. The revolt was confined largely to North India.
4. Most of India remained neutral.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are cited as limitations: the revolt lacked a common goal, modern nationalism was not yet developed, its main spread was in North India, and most of India remained neutral.
accepted.tq: Test the complete set of qualifications rather than selecting only the geographical limitation.

accepted.s: Which of the following groups was specifically identified as largely uninvolved in the Revolt of 1857?
accepted.x: The elite and urban classes were largely uninvolved, which is one reason historians question whether the revolt can be called a fully national movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the social group omitted from the main participation pattern.

accepted.s: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels' articles on the uprising were compiled under which title?
o: The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857
Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies
The First Indian War of Independence 1857-1859
accepted.x: Karl Marx's and Friedrich Engels' articles were compiled as The First Indian War of Independence 1857-1859.
accepted.tq: Match the compilation title with the pair of writers associated with it.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of publication:
A. The Indian War of Independence, 1857
B. The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857
C. Eighteen Fifty-Seven
D. The First Indian War of Independence 1857-1859
accepted.x: The Indian War of Independence, 1857 was published in 1909; the Marx-Engels compilation covers 1857-1859; and both Majumdar's and Sen's books were published in 1957. Thus the order is A, D, B, C.
accepted.tq: Fix the early 1909 work first and then place the 1957 centenary works.
